name: Hitachi Energy India Ltd
title: Hitachi Energy India Ltd - 543187 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Hitachi Energy India Q1 FY27: revenue up 68.6% YoY to INR 2,493.7 crs; orders INR 5,096.5 crs with backlog at INR 32,222.1 crs.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 68.6% YoY to INR 2,493.7 crs, driven by execution of the existing backlog. Operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs, including a INR 36.37 crs unrealised forex loss, and PBT rose 120.2% YoY. Order intake was INR 5,096.5 crs; excluding the large Q1 FY26 HVDC order, orders grew 26.1% YoY and 39.7% QoQ. Management said gross margin fell YoY on product mix but improved QoQ. The quarter's wins included a first BESS order, a Europe grid-link order and data-centre orders.

financial_highlights.change: +26.1% YoY and +39.7% QoQ excluding HVDC (comparable basis)
+135.0% YoY; includes unrealised forex loss of INR 36.37 crs

segments.name: Product orders
segments.commentary: Management said product orders were the largest contributor in Q1 FY27; the order book is diversified across end-markets and EPC and OEM channels.

segments.name: Utilities and HVDC
segments.commentary: Management named Utilities and HVDC as core businesses. A large HVDC order of about INR 1,700 crs was in the quarter, and the Khavda HVDC project is ramping while Bhadla is starting.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Services business unit was described as focused on continuity and resilience of the installed base; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the HVDC revenue contribution to build in years two and three, with first-year execution on the lower side.
A greenfield HVDC project is under bidding and is expected to be awarded in about six months.
Railway projects are progressing slower than planned and are expected to pick up in the second half of FY27; transmission weakness is described as timing-related.
Karjan (Vadodara) transformer factory, the company's 20th manufacturing facility, began construction in June 2026 with targeted commissioning in December 2028.
Data-centre visibility is described as strong; management referenced a 15 GW by 2030 opportunity, contingent on government support.
capex_capacity: 20th manufacturing facility at Karjan, Vadodara: construction began June 2026; targeted commissioning December 2028; designed as a fully digital and smart factory.
Capex is aimed at capacity expansion and localising components toward end-to-end manufacturing in India; no capex amount was disclosed.
BESS offering is modular and containerised, excluding batteries; PCS is not yet localised and localisation of BESS is still needed.
Depreciation rose QoQ on ongoing capex for capacity expansion; finance cost broadly stable.
demand_pricing: Order wins included a 2 GW wind evacuation order in Europe (three transmission links delivering 6 GW; value about INR 1,700 crs per management, a combination of three orders with a services focus), a 165 MW / 330 MWh BESS in Andhra Pradesh, and 400 kV GIS/GIB for a 100 GW solar park in western India.
Multiple data-centre orders from hyperscalers, including a 40 x 2,500 kVA project in Hyderabad.
Material costs as a percentage of revenue stayed within the historical range; management said 60-65% of orders are pass-through and there was no material commodity impact this quarter.
Management said the entry of Chinese players in GIS and transformers is not expected to have a material impact, citing existing competition in other forms; no major threat from TBEA.
Gross margin fell YoY on product mix (management did not give quantum) but improved QoQ, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value of the Europe 2 GW order and the export share?
qa_highlights.answer: The Europe order is a combination of three orders valued at about INR 1,700 crs, with services and support focus. Export contribution to revenue is around 25%, which is the current run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin contraction YoY of over 350 bps: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin improved QoQ and only slightly contracted YoY, mainly due to product mix; the quantum was not given.

qa_highlights.question: BESS offering, competition and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Offering is a modular, scalable, end-to-end solution excluding batteries, with digital layers and battery management integration. Margin profile is hard to state yet as the technology matures and localisation is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 FY27 revenue comes from HVDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a breakup; said there is some HVDC contribution, with full contribution expected in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre order size and momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Multiple data-centre orders rather than one large order; visibility is strong, with long-lead items such as GIS and dry transformers being secured by customers. Management referenced 15 GW by 2030 if government support continues.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity price exposure outside transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: No material impact this quarter; 60-65% of orders are pass-through and small impacts can be managed.

risks_watch: Gross margin trajectory: YoY contraction on product mix, and the margin profile of the new BESS business has not been quantified.
HVDC revenue ramp is back-ended; execution of Khavda and Bhadla is a key monitor.
Competitive intensity from Chinese entrants in GIS and transformers and the 60-65% local content rule; no quantified impact.
Railway order slowdown, expected to recover in H2 FY27, and transmission timing.
Unrealised forex and commodity losses (INR 36.37 crs in Q1).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with a stated expectation that margin ambitions will be met. Evasive on specifics: management declined to give HVDC backlog share, HVDC revenue contribution, BESS margins, segment-wise value of the Kinet Railway opportunity, and the quantum of YoY gross margin change.
key_quotes: We have started the FY27 on a strong note, delivering robust growth in both orders and revenues.
On a comparable basis, order intake in Q1 FY27 increased by 26.1% YoY and 39.7% QoQ
Our strong order backlog, combined with a healthy bidding pipeline, provides good visibility for future revenue growth.
60%-65% of our orders are pass through. In this quarter, there is no commodity impact per se.

adds.what: 20th manufacturing facility at Karjan, Vadodara (fully digital smart factory)

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; backlog of INR 32,222 crs and Q1 revenue +68.6% YoY support near-term growth, with HVDC revenue building in years two and three and Karjan plant not live until Dec 2028 (about 10 quarters).
